why:
I checked the briefs against all three must_catch items, and all three are handled.
1. Builder brief: step 2 says "keep the current comma behaviour exactly as it is". Step 3 says "Keep the existing tests passing" and step 5 says "Run npm test and make sure every test passes". Neither expect line asks for this, so the item holds.
2. Verifier brief: npm test and plain CSV behaviour appear only under "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)". It says "Run npm test and report whether it passes" and suggests a check that CSV output is unchanged. It never states in so many words that no expect line covers these. But it places them outside the gates and marks them as advice, which handles the trap. This is the closest call of the three.
3. Check 1 runs TSV/CSV pairs of the same table, for example 'a	b
1	2
' with --tsv against 'a,b
1,2
' with the plain command. It then compares the two JSON arrays for deep equality.
